body.x: INTERPOL is the world’s largest international police organization, with 196 Member Countries. Created in 1923, it facilitates cross-border police co-operation, and supports and assists all organizations, authorities, and services whose mission is to prevent or combat international crime.

INTERPOL actively encourages applications from women and nationals of member countries that are currently unrepresented among our staff (please click on this link to access the list of countries). Candidates from these countries are particularly encouraged to apply.
INTERPOL’s recruitment process is merit-based hence all hiring decisions are made considering the applicant’s qualifications and the needs of the Organization.
Reporting To: Assistant Director, Building and Global Facilities

Only professional experience for which candidates can provide official proof of employment will be considered. Candidates could be requested to provide copies of such official documents prior to interviews/test.
* Subsequent extension to this post will be subject to the terms of the Organization’s Staff Manual, to satisfactory performance and to availability of funds.

Tests/interviews in connection to this selection procedure will take place approximately 3-4 weeks after the deadline for applications. Applicants are kindly requested to plan their availability during this period accordingly, in case they are short-listed.
Selected candidates will be expected to report for duty approximately two to three months after receiving an offer of employment at the latest.
This selection exercise may be used to generate a reserve list of suitable candidates that may be used to address Organization's similar staffing needs in the future.
DUTIES, INCLUDING GOALS AND OBJECTIVES OF THE POST

The Executive Directorate Resource Management (EDRM) enables INTERPOL’s global mission through the effective management of its financial, human and corporate resources. Within EDRM, Buildings – Global Facilities is responsible for creating and managing secure, modern and fit-for-purpose facilities across the Organization, including the delivery of the Lyon Headquarters Building Extension and Renovation Programme.

Reporting to the Assistant Director Building and Global Facilities, the Senior Coordinator Building Extension and Renovation Programme’s main activity is to lead the Organization in realizing the construction of the extension of the Organization’s Headquarters and the associated renovations of the current premises. The Senior Coordinator of the Building Extension and Renovation Programme will be responsible for INTERPOL requirements, monitoring and supervising the construction, renovation and restructuring project, and coordinating the associated projects linked to the relocation of staff during the construction period, ensuring overall programme coherence, effective governance, coordination across internal functions, business continuity and the successful transition to the new facilities.
Formulate the strategy for the building extension and renovation programme and develop clear goals that are consistent with the agreed strategy.

Supervise and ensure effective and efficient execution of projects within the programme, ensuring on-time delivery, within scope and budget, following the Project Management Guidelines and methodology.

Oversee the development of the programme ensuring coordination amongst the various projects in the framework of the programme, including the identification and management of interdependencies across projects and relevant internal functions.

Ensure effective programme governance, including the preparation of decisions, timely escalation of issues, monitoring of agreed actions and follow-up on decisions taken by the relevant governance bodies.
Provide programme planning adjustments (by modifying the scope, schedule or budget when necessary) and initiate exception reports and applicable project(s) revisions.
Review progress made, problems encountered and concerns identified and take appropriate action to address issues and to ensure that projects are achieving their set targets.
Promote synergy across the projects/programme in terms of lessons learned, maintaining coherence in implementation.
Develop project documentation ensuring regular reporting to hierarchy and different stakeholders according to the needs of the Organization.

Develop multi-annual work plans and structuring of operational delivery arrangements, ensuring the integration of construction, relocation, business continuity, change management and communication activities into the overall programme planning..

Identify, assess, plan and implement risk management procedures. Elaborate mitigation plans, including risks affecting operational continuity during construction and the transition to the new facilities.

Continuously analyze the programme’s context (internal and external) assessing pertinence and taking appropriate action to ensure continued alignment with the Organization’s goals and strategic framework.

Bring projects within the programme to a closure, conducting project/programme performance evaluation and capturing lessons learned, including the coordination of handover arrangements and the transition to operational use of the new and renovated facilities.
Lead, manage and guide project teams, making optimal use of allocated resources.
Delegate the appropriate responsibility and accountability to project/programme teams.
Ensure roles, responsibilities and reporting lines are clear to project/programme teams.
Accurately judge the amount of time and resources needed to accomplish tasks and matches tasks to skills, ensure accountability for results, and actively support career development.
Monitor progress against milestones and deadlines, ensuring timely follow-up on deliverables, decisions and dependencies across project teams and contributing functions..
Guide the respective project managers and their teams to share a common strategy and performance standards.
Supervise several projects / project managers/senior project managers.
Oversee the effective management of the allocated financial resources to the programme in line with INTERPOL financial rules and regulations, ensuring accountability for their appropriate use.
Monitor and meet financial exigencies, identifying appropriate solutions to emerging constraints.
Monitor expenditures to ensure that they remain within authorized levels and take corrective action where necessary.
Oversee the accurate and complete financial reporting ensuring that all relevant records are maintained and any discrepancies appropriately addressed .
Monitor the implementation of transactions with regard to regulatory standards addressing or escalating compliance issues as appropriate.
Oversee resource-mobilization efforts and identify solutions to addresss potential budget deficits and equipment needs.

Create all management documentation with a programmatic approach in accordance with Project Management guidelines, including consolidated programme plans, governance documentation, decision records, and action-tracking mechanisms.

Gather the real estate needs of the Organization’s internal services and partners and their formulation to the department responsible for the operation. Communication of the French Government lead’s requests to the Organization’s decision-making bodies.

During the initiation phase of new projects (or follow-up projects), produce (in collaboration with the different business areas) business cases (concept notes, project proposals) including budget and resource estimates with a programmatic approach. Involve relevant stakeholders in order to support the definition of the project programme and objectives.

Manage support needs from legal and financial departments, and coordinate contributions from other relevant internal functions to ensure alignment of requirements, timelines, and operational dependencies.

Lead on all phases of the project, including needs analysis, programme definition, design, engagement in selection processes where relevant, delivery relocation planning, operational readiness, handover and transition to the new facilities.

Coordinate with relevant internal functions to ensure that business continuity requirements are identified, planned and appropriately addressed throughout construction, renovation and relocation activities.
Develop and provide the necessary reporting documents as need be, ensuring that programme-level risks, dependencies, decisions and outstanding actions are clearly identified and followed up.
In accordance with INTERPOL Strategy, promote the programme’s value outside the Organization and collaborate effectively with project stakeholders;

Communicate programme objectives, achievements and activities to relevant stakeholders within the Organization (management, staff, administration), in coordination with the function responsible for programme communication and change management.

Support senior management in reporting to the steering committee with France (COSTRA) and the Organization’s governing bodies, including the preparation of matters requiring decisions and follow-up on agreed actions.
Draft updates on engagement with the French Government and updates on programme progress for INTERPOL senior management and governing bodies.
Ensure buy-in and constant support of units involved within the Organization, facilitating their coordinated contribution to programme planning, implementation and transition activities.

Ensure that change management and communication activities, led by the designated responsible function, are effectively integrated into programme planning, governance, milestones and delivery, in coordination with the relevant stakeholders.
Keep beneficiary country, donors and other key stakeholders informed of progress or setbacks in projects/programme.
Provide support in the overall development and implementation of the unit’s activities.
Perform all other functions, duties, and responsibilities that may be necessary to ensure the smooth functioning of the Directorate/programme Team as required by the hierarchy.
6. Perform any other duties as required by the hierarchy.

Five years’ education at an accredited University Technical Diploma or other specialized higher education establishment in a relevant field (eg. construction, public works, civil engineering, architecture).
Certification in the field of project management from certified institutes or proven experience leading similar size programmes.

At least eight years’ experience managing projects/programmes of increased value/complexity, in the field of construction/building industry , including experience in overall programme coordination, governance and management of interdependent projects and stakeholders.

Experience coordinating multidisciplinary teams and internal functions, including managing operational dependencies and supporting business continuity and transition arrangements in complex programmes.
In-depth knowledge of French regulations in the construction field (urban planning, building licence, etc.) is required.
Experience dealing with French authorities at different levels (local, national) is required.
In-depth knowledge of the regulations on French public procurement contracts, in particular in the field of construction and complex global contract-type procedures would be an asset.
Knowledge of real estate law/property management/law and public procurement in France would be an asset.
Professional fluency in English and French (written and oral).
Ability to maintain objectivity and apply logical, specifically inductive, reasoning.
Ability to work in teams as well as individually.
Ability to synthesize and organize data.
Ability to work persistently and under pressure.
Ability to solve problems quickly and effectively.
Ability to resolve conflict to reach mutual consensus.
As part of our commitment to transparency throughout our recruitment process, INTERPOL's Staff Manual Regulation 11.4: Age-limit, which states that:

'Officials of the Organization shall not normally be retained in service beyond the age of 65 years. The Secretary General may, in exceptional cases and in the interests of the Organization, extend this age limit, in which case he shall inform the official concerned sufficiently in advance.'

Given this Regulation and in case candidates reach the age of 65 during the potential duration of the appointment, should they be selected for the position and the process proceed to appointment, the employment period may be affected by this regulatory limit and may therefore not extend for the full standard contract duration as published in the vacancy notice.
We are sharing this information to ensure transparency at this stage of the process.
This position is no longer open.
